source: Puma et al. (2012), Third Grade Follow-up to the Head Start Impact Study: Final Report, OPRE 2012-45; rendered Exhibits 4.3, 4.7, and 4.9 (printed pp. 81, 87, and 89).
scope: Four additional statistically significant third-grade findings for the 4-year-old cohort and their IOT counterparts. Each pair is one outcome from the same randomized access study; the IOT result scales the access effect for participation and is not another study.

rows.ittName: For children entering Head Start at age four, the third-grade total-problem-behavior ITT impact was -0.50 points (p = .090).
rows.ittDescription: Lower scores indicate fewer reported behavior problems on this parent-reported measure. This suggestive result is one outcome from the same cohort and is not independent evidence alongside its IOT counterpart.
rows.ittUnit: Regression-adjusted parent-reported total-problem-behavior ITT difference at third grade, Head Start access minus control; 4-year-old cohort; lower is more favorable.
rows.iotName: For children entering Head Start at age four, the third-grade total-problem-behavior IOT impact was -0.75 points (p = .090).
rows.iotDescription: Lower scores indicate fewer reported behavior problems on this parent-reported measure. This treatment-on-the-treated estimate is the participation-scaled counterpart of the paired ITT result, not independent corroboration.
rows.iotUnit: Regression-adjusted parent-reported total-problem-behavior treatment-on-the-treated impact at third grade; 4-year-old cohort; lower is more favorable.

rows.ittName: For children entering Head Start at age four, the third-grade closeness-with-teacher ITT impact was -0.67 points (p = .060).
rows.ittDescription: Lower scores are less favorable on this teacher-reported relationship measure. This suggestive result is reporter-specific and remains paired with its IOT counterpart rather than treated as a separate study.
rows.ittUnit: Regression-adjusted teacher-reported closeness-with-teacher ITT difference at third grade, Head Start access minus control; 4-year-old cohort; lower is less favorable.
rows.iotName: For children entering Head Start at age four, the third-grade closeness-with-teacher IOT impact was -1.00 points (p = .060).
rows.iotDescription: Lower scores are less favorable on this teacher-reported relationship measure. This treatment-on-the-treated estimate is the participation-scaled counterpart of the paired ITT result, not independent corroboration.
rows.iotUnit: Regression-adjusted teacher-reported closeness-with-teacher treatment-on-the-treated impact at third grade; 4-year-old cohort; lower is less favorable.

rows.ittName: For children entering Head Start at age four, the third-grade positive-teacher-child-relationship ITT impact was -1.33 points (p = .063).
rows.ittDescription: Lower scores are less favorable on this teacher-reported relationship measure. This suggestive result is distinct from parents’ reports and is not a separate study from its IOT counterpart.
rows.ittUnit: Regression-adjusted teacher-reported positive-teacher-child-relationship ITT difference at third grade, Head Start access minus control; 4-year-old cohort; lower is less favorable.
rows.iotName: For children entering Head Start at age four, the third-grade positive-teacher-child-relationship IOT impact was -1.99 points (p = .063).
rows.iotDescription: Lower scores are less favorable on this teacher-reported relationship measure. This treatment-on-the-treated estimate is the participation-scaled counterpart of the paired ITT result, not independent corroboration.
rows.iotUnit: Regression-adjusted teacher-reported positive-teacher-child-relationship treatment-on-the-treated impact at third grade; 4-year-old cohort; lower is less favorable.

rows.ittName: For children entering Head Start at age four, parents reported a +0.27 third-grade ITT impact on time spent with their child (p = .001).
rows.ittDescription: Higher scores are favorable on this parent-reported measure. It is one parenting-practice outcome from the 4-year-old cohort, not a child academic or health result.
rows.ittUnit: Regression-adjusted parent-reported time-spent-with-child ITT difference at third grade, Head Start access minus control; 4-year-old cohort; higher is more favorable.
rows.iotName: For children entering Head Start at age four, parents reported a +0.40 third-grade IOT impact on time spent with their child (p = .001).
rows.iotDescription: Higher scores are favorable on this parent-reported measure. This treatment-on-the-treated estimate is the participation-scaled counterpart of the paired ITT result, not independent corroboration.
rows.iotUnit: Regression-adjusted parent-reported time-spent-with-child treatment-on-the-treated impact at third grade; 4-year-old cohort; higher is more favorable.
